subject: Pricing & next steps - committed use options (Novaflow)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@novaflow.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T15:10:00Z
Subject: Pricing & next steps - committed use options (Novaflow)

Hi Ethan — great to meet today. Quick recap and action items from our discovery: 

Call recap (high level):
- Primary workload: real-time semantic search + summarization for customer support.
- Expected traffic profile: steady baseline with weekly spikes.
- Current integration target: Q1 pilot (small subset), full rollout target in Q2.

Pricing / cost qualification you shared:
- Estimated token volume: ~4–6B tokens / month (mix of short + long contexts).
- Budget range: roughly $40k–$60k / month initially; potential to ramp.
- Target unit economics: you mentioned aiming for something in the ~$8–$12 per 1M tokens neighborhood (target $/1M tokens).

Requested from you: confirmation of the token estimate above and any internal procurement windows/decision timeline (you mentioned end of Nov for a commercial decision).

What we will do next: 
1) I’m attaching a draft term sheet that outlines committed-use tiers and starter credits so you can see effective $/1M numbers (Redwood-TermSheet-Draft-commitment.pdf).
2) If the token estimate above is accurate, we’ll model three committed-use options (3mo, 12mo, multi-year) and surface the effective $/1M tokens for each.
3) We’ll include startup program options if Novaflow qualifies (VC-backed, <24 months revenue) — that typically gives short-term credits and a heavier ramp incentive.

Next steps for you: please confirm the ~4–6B tokens/mo estimate and the Nov decision timeline. If you can share the short token breakdown (search vs. summarize) that helps refine the effective unit price.

Attachments: Novaflow_MA_Pricing_Reqs.pdf (from your team earlier), Redwood-TermSheet-Draft-commitment.pdf (attached).

Thanks — I’ll loop in finance and Marissa internally once you confirm numbers so we can get a firm commercial offer over to you.

Best,
Ben

Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@novaflow.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T11:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Pricing & next steps - committed use options (Novaflow)

Ben — thanks for the recap, that aligns with my notes. A couple of clarifications and asks from my side: 

1) Token breakdown: roughly 70% short queries (search embeddings + short prompts, ~60–80 tokens each), 30% longer summarization (avg ~800 tokens). The 4–6B is vaulted across both workloads.
2) Budget: $40k–$60k/month is what procurement has penciled, but leadership is targeting a target $/1M tokens that ends up around $9–10 to make our unit economics work at scale.
3) We’re an early-stage company (Series A, VC-backed). Curious what the startup program would look like (credits vs. % off committed tiers). Also want to understand multi-year incentives — we could do 24 months if the economics make sense.

Decision timeline: we’re aiming to choose a vendor and sign terms before Dec 15, ideally sooner if the pricing aligns.

I’m attaching a short spreadsheet with our internal token projection and ramp (Novaflow_pricing_constraints.xlsx). Can you confirm: what’s Redwood’s baseline list price per 1M tokens for the model class we discussed, and what effective rates you can get us to with committed-use and startup options?

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Cole
Head of ML Engineering, Novaflow
ethan.cole@novaflow.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pricing & next steps - committed use options (Novaflow)

Ethan — thanks for the detail and for the sheet. Based on the 70/30 split and the 4–6B/mo projection, here’s a practical proposal that balances your target unit economics and our cost structure: 

Baseline (model class we discussed, on-demand): $12.00 per 1M tokens (this is our public on-demand reference for that model tier).

Committed-use tiers (effective prices shown):
- 3 month commitment, 4B tokens/mo: 15% off base -> $10.20 / 1M tokens (effective)
- 12 month commitment, 4B tokens/mo: 30% off base -> $8.40 / 1M tokens (effective)
- 24 month commitment, 4B tokens/mo: 35% off base -> $7.80 / 1M tokens (effective)

Notes:
- Tiering scales: if you ramp to 6B/mo we can model a blended effective price that keeps you around the same or slightly better effective $/1M with a higher absolute commit.
- Startup program: because you’re Series A and VC-backed, we can add a startup incentive: 3 months of credits covering up to 50% of usage costs (applies to first 3 months of committed use) + a waived onboarding credit. That effectively reduces your first-quarter blended cost significantly.
- Multi-year incentive: the 35% for 24mo is conditional on an annual billing prepay or a standard invoiced ARR contract with finance approval. Finance will request basic credit references.

Example math (12mo / 4B):
- Base monthly list = 4,000 (million tokens) * $12 = $48,000
- After 30% committed discount -> $33,600 (effective $/1M = $8.40)
- With startup first-quarter credits applied (if eligible), Q1 net could be ~50% lower depending on usage shape.

Attachments: I’m re-attaching the draft term sheet with these bands filled in — Redwood-TermSheet-Draft-commitment.pdf. If this lines up with your expectations I can: 
1) Get internal signoff (Marissa) on the 12mo and 24mo special pricing bands,
2) Pull finance into the thread to confirm billing/prepay flow and required docs,
3) Send a DocuSign-ready term sheet.

Next step: can you confirm which commitment length (3/12/24) you prefer for the modeled 4–6B/mo case and whether you want prepay or invoiced billing? Also confirm eligibility for the startup credits (one-line about VC/backing and age).

Thanks — I’ll hold off on escalating to finance until you confirm.

Best,
Ben
